cotton.description: A soft, fluffy staple fiber that grows in a boll around the seeds of the cotton plants. It provides a breathable, comfortable fabric heavily used in daily wear.

silk.description: A natural protein fiber produced by silkworms, known for its high luster, strength, and luxurious feel. It is a staple of premium festive wear.

wool.description: A textile fiber obtained from sheep and other animals, offering excellent insulation and warmth for colder climates.

linen.description: A textile made from the fibers of the flax plant, known for its exceptional coolness and freshness in hot and humid weather.

synthetic_blend.description: A mix of natural fibers and man-made synthetic fibers like polyester or nylon. It often mimics natural fabrics but is cheaper and more durable.

tussar_silk.description: Also known as wild silk, produced by silkworms that feed on trees like Sal and Arjun. It has a rich texture, natural dull gold sheen, and distinct uneven feel.

muga_silk.description: A rare, wild silk unique to Assam, renowned for its naturally yellowish-golden tint and extreme durability that outlasts the wearer.
